title: performance-canary: adaptive-kv-hysteresis-and-auto-detection-rollout-guards
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: our performance canary system occasionally surfaces spurious latency/throughput regressions during bursty workloads and KV cache population storms. This PR implements an adaptive hysteresis layer and KV-sensitive thresholds that reduce false-positive rollouts while preserving quick detection for real regressions.

What changed (single-line description): add adaptive hysteresis controller, KV-population detector, per-route hysteresis profiles, and rollout guard tuning + tests and docs.

Details: This change introduces an AdaptiveHysteresis controller into the perf-canary service. It adjusts regression detection thresholds using short-term and medium-term latency baselines and KV cache population signals. When the KV throttling/population metric is high, the controller increases hysteresis and widens latency windows to avoid transient alerts. We also added per-route profiles so high-variance routes (e.g., long-tail completion routes) are less sensitive by default. The rollout guard policy now has a new state machine: pass -> degraded -> quarantine -> rollback. Quarantine holds a small percentage of traffic for extended observation rather than immediate rollback.

Checklist:
- [x] Add AdaptiveHysteresis algorithm and config knobs
- [x] Add KVPopulationDetector and sensor for kv_cache_fill_rate metric
- [x] Add per-route profile support and default profiles
- [x] Unit and integration tests for controller logic
- [x] End-to-end perf canary integration test in perf-canary-lab
- [x] Console docs: rollout guard states and recommended profiles
- [x] Backwards-compatible config parsing for older rollout policies

Risk: low-medium. Behavior is behind a feature flag (perf_canary.adaptive_kv_hysteresis = true) and default off for existing customers. We validated on staging with synthetic bursty workload and representative production traces.

Testing notes: added deterministic unit tests for threshold adaptation, mocked kv metrics for population storm scenarios, and a canary scenario test that simulates a regression vs a KV-population storm. Manual staging run attached below.

Related: builds on work from ENG-5872 (auto-detect hysteresis) and addresses customer incident SUP-3142 where a cache warmup caused a large rollback during a model rollout.

release_notes: Added adaptive hysteresis and KV-population-aware thresholds to performance canary. New rollout guard state 'quarantine' holds a small portion of traffic for extended observation. Feature gated behind perf_canary.adaptive_kv_hysteresis (default off). Recommended: enable in staging and tune per-route profiles before enabling in production.
staging_run_summary: Staging run 2026-02-22: synthetic burst (1M reqs over 1h) with KV population spikes. With adaptive hysteresis enabled, canary moved to quarantine at 3% traffic and stabilized after 12 minutes; no rollback triggered. Baseline false-positive rate reduced from 1.9% to 0.2% in test traces.
notes: Feature is backward-compatible and controlled via feature flag. Operations should monitor perf-canary.adaptive_kv_hysteresis rollout metrics and adjust per-route sensitivity. Will follow up with rollout playbook updates.
